title: Mirabel and the Summit
premise: Dominic Hartwell, a riverboat captain who has spent a decade outrunning her past, takes a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to reach the wreck of the Mirabel before the salvage fleet does. The map leads not just to sunken gold but to evidence that Dominic's own family helped sink the ship and silence its crew. Racing six tides against fleet boss Cassian Voss, she must decide whether survival means staying invisible or surfacing with the truth. In the end, Dominic scuttles the salvage operation, gives the gold to the wreck's surviving descendants, and finally claims her own name on the river.
about_author: Ivo Sandoval is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent seven years working freight runs on inland waterways before writing full-time. Their fiction draws on river lore, salvage culture, and the quiet ethics of people who live by the current.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A storm-stranded prospector named Edda collapses aboard Dominic's boat and trades a hand-drawn map of the wreck of the Mirabel for a promise: beat the salvage fleet there. Dominic wants no part of it, but Edda dies holding her hand, and the promise sticks like a splinter. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation born from guilt over promises once broken.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic calculates the tide windows and realizes the fleet will arrive first unless she cuts through forbidden shallows. Her deckhand, Juno, warns that Voss's scouts are already buying fuel downriver. Dominic studies the map and finds Edda's marginal note: 'They didn't sink on their own.' Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, flashback woven through. Running the night channel, Dominic recalls how she vanished ten years ago after her father's shipping company collapsed amid scandal. The map's coordinates brush against waters her father's barges once worked, an unwelcome coincidence. Emotional beat: the past surfacing like a hull she can't keep bailed dry.

chapters.title: Voss at the Fuel Dock
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At a refueling stop, salvage boss Cassian Voss buys her a drink and offers triple rate for any 'local knowledge' about the Mirabel. He mentions Edda by name and calls her a thief. Dominic lies smoothly, hating how easily the old skills return. Emotional beat: the seduction and danger of being seen.

chapters.title: The Shallows Run
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Juno narrates the harrowing night run through unmarked shallows, grounding nearly twice while Dominic reads the water like scripture. They find Edda's hidden cache boat, stocked with dive gear and a journal naming names—including one spelled 'Hartwell.' Emotional beat: trust between captain and crew tested and proven.

chapters.title: Edda's Journal
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The journal reveals the Mirabel was deliberately scuttled to bury evidence of insurance fraud, and Dominic's father signed off on it. She rages, grieves, and almost burns the map. Juno talks her down: the descendants of the drowned crew deserve the truth more than Dominic deserves her invisibility. Emotional beat: identity cracking open under hard light.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Voss's lead vessel ambushes them at the narrows; a boarding skirmish leaves Juno injured and Dominic's engine sabotaged. Voss offers her a last out—walk away, keep her name clean. She refuses, and he takes her boat's papers hostage. Emotional beat: cornered defiance; the price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: Down to the Mirabel
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. With hours left, Dominic free-dives the wreck alone, finding the strongbox and, wedged beside it, a child's shoe—one of the crew brought family aboard. The sight transforms the mission from treasure to testimony. Above, Voss's divers enter the water. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Climax. Dominic surfaces into Voss's waiting net, fights him across the flooded cargo deck as the tide turns, and uses the wreck's shifting ballast to trap his salvage rig against a piling. She radios the coast authority with the journal's evidence, sacrificing the gold's secrecy to make the record public. Emotional beat: power refused at personal cost.

chapters.title: A Name on the Water
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Weeks later, the inquiry vindicates the Mirabel's crew; the gold goes to their descendants, and Dominic testifies under her full name for the first time in ten years. She repaints her boat's stern with new lettering—Mirabel's Wake—and signs the harbor registry without flinching. Emotional beat: belonging earned, invisibility voluntarily surrendered.
